cause: Per-frame PNG data URLs loaded by SVG/image elements are repeated in Chromium Network events, saturating the native CDP connection and queuing screenshot/layout/input commands.
scope: local raster preview and its compositor; default canvas renderer and motion algorithms unchanged by this correction
redAssertion: frame PNGs must not flood CDP as data URLs: 217 !== 0

hypotheses.name: CDP event traffic accumulation
hypotheses.result: confirmed by request URL volume, increasing protocol RTT, unchanged original seven checks passing after correction

hypotheses.name: window focus or visibility
hypotheses.result: not observed in the failing profiled run

hypotheses.name: post-resume geometry or hit ordering
hypotheses.result: standalone drag succeeds; failed run can stall before suspend; original post-resume drag and physical cursor checks both pass after frame loading correction

fix: decode frame PNG bytes directly into ImageBitmap and close both layers after paint, stale-frame discard or decode failure
use one owned SVG Blob URL per raster figure, revoking on replacement, remount, snapshot and disposal
regression: existing seven native assertions pass unchanged after runtime fix
maintained native suite adds zero PNG data-URL traffic assertion and positive Blob traffic observation
unit test exercises bounded URL ownership across actual figure draws, disposal and remount
native suite records current phase and per-check times, has a 120-second total deadline, restores physical cursor and removes isolated profile
limits: controlled suspend is not real OS sleep/lock
not three-platform CI or long-duration resource acceptance
